questions.q: What does COALESCE(expr1, expr2, expr3) return?
options: NULL if any one of the three is NULL
Always the first expression, regardless of its value
The sum of all three expressions
The first of the three expressions that isn't NULL
questions.explain: COALESCE checks its arguments left to right and returns the first one that is not NULL.

questions.q: How many arguments can COALESCE accept?
options: Exactly three, always
Any number — it isn't limited to two
Up to four and no more
Exactly two, always
questions.explain: Unlike a strictly two-argument function, COALESCE can chain as many fallback candidates as needed.

questions.q: In COALESCE(pp.PhoneNumber, ea.EmailAddress, 'No contact on file'), when does the result become 'No contact on file'?
options: Whenever EmailAddress is NULL, regardless of PhoneNumber
Whenever PhoneNumber is NULL, regardless of EmailAddress
Never — the literal is unreachable
Only when both PhoneNumber and EmailAddress are NULL
questions.explain: COALESCE only falls through to a later argument when every argument before it is NULL.

questions.q: Why does COALESCE(Freight, 0) help inside a calculation?
options: It rounds Freight to the nearest whole number
NULL propagates through arithmetic, so wrapping a possibly-NULL operand keeps the whole expression from becoming NULL
It converts Freight to a string automatically
It removes the Freight column from the result
questions.explain: NULL + anything is NULL, so replacing a NULL Freight with 0 first prevents that from silently wiping out a calculation.

questions.q: When is the only time COALESCE itself returns NULL?
options: When every single argument passed to it is NULL
When the first argument is NULL, even if later ones aren't
COALESCE never returns NULL under any circumstance
When there are fewer than three arguments
questions.explain: COALESCE only returns NULL if it never finds a non-NULL value anywhere in its argument list.
